[quote=democratic_sanguivallis;60760258][spoiler=[b]Citharo the Beautiful[/b]][b]Citharo the Beautiful[/b]

After the revolution, the old gives way to the new. It's why people presume the architect of socialist states to be miserable, imaged as lines of concrete boxes through the grey jungle, sometimes decrepit, unsuitable for human habitation. But these same boxes are often utilitarian, which provided men and women with inexpensive housing, and often state-subsidized under the fundamental rights guaranteed by most socialist governments. However, perhaps as an indication of its sheer ideological immensity, what greeted you in Citharo was not the utilitarian housing of the new but instead the ornaments and beauty of the old, dressed in marble and limestone and with gilded carvings resting on warm Marisalbic sunlight.

"City Beautiful", as the Vespurian architects would call it.

Enter through the port and walk along the pier, and you'll be met by the "Twelve Apostles", twelve great roads that form along the Cisalpine Highway leading deeper into Citharo's center, each one leading visitors through a different aspect of city life. Along San Filippo's, for example, would be the oldest shops in the city, some with a legacy going back to the Vallist Kingdom, and which leads directly towards the great Alpine Highway that guided travelers to the capital city of Ventusia. In San Simone, there are a row of old entertainment buildings once known for its gambling and gentleman's clubs, though these had long since been converted into multi-purpose halls instead for various community events. 

The Thyvenic delegation would be driven through the sixth street, Sant'Andrea, where St. Andrew's crosses and saltires appear prominently throughout the stuccoworks that lined its high-rise buildings. A few landmarks are seen here and there, such as the prominent [i]Ciotola d'oro[/i] hotel, the [i]San Michele Confessore[/i] building, the "King Fir" tree that acted as a natural separator for private and public buildings, and last but not least the [i]Municipio[/i], the seat of Citharo's local government and, nowadays, the [i]de facto[/i] meeting place of the Socialist International (who [i]de jure[/i] are supposed to use the nearby building instead, San Martino's.

"Yo."

A strange woman wearing thick black sunglasses greeted the limousine as it parked to the side of the Municipio. In her hand was a thick set of papers stapled poorly together, seemingly done with great difficult, for the corners of the documents had been haphazardly crimpled perhaps during the effort. It was Immacolata Terrasi, one of Socialist International's foremost economic experts. Why she was standing outside without ceremony or guards, and holding on to what seemed to be a very important reports, only God seems to know. Judging by the lack of the crowd, it seems that the Sanguinians declined to make the meeting publicly-known too, and it seems the domestic media narrative had been focused almost entirely on keeping track of the Thyvenic Revolution [i]beyond[/i] the nation's borders.

"Thyven delegation, welcome to Citharo!" Terrasi loudly proclaimed, crossing her arms and damaging her report even further. "Good morning, good morning! I am Immocolata Terrasi, I was sent here by the Presidium to meet with you all. You're walking on Socialism's most Holy land, so make sure to bask in the atmosphere! C'mon, follow me, we can talk about things inside."

Before the Thyvenic delegation could even introduce themselves, Terrasi suddenly turned around and began marching into the Municipio, the two Red Guards meekly opening the doors for her as though she were a member of the party elite, and she was, though she didn't seem the slightest bit concerned about presenting herself in that way.[/spoiler][/quote]

The Thrømm are naturally a polite and reserved people, not as aristocratic as the Montfleurois, trending to be a bit more provincial, thus while the casual attitude of Terrasi was perhaps unusual, it wasnt improper.

Piter Drømm and Erjk Malben had little to say yet, instead quietly approving of the city, thus as a result they took a moment to get out of the car, their antlered forms perhaps giving pause to the locals, for sanguivallis was not known for Thrømm tourism.

"... Tough crowd..."

Terrasi shrugged off her guests' silence and quietly guided them deeper into the Municipio. Normally, when you enter a Sanguinian city hall, you are met by a wide open square that formed the central lobby of the area. 

"We used to call it a forum like in the old days." Terrasi explained, pointing at the floor as if the marbled tiling were something unusual to the Thyvenic delegation. "Some still call this a forum, but the Social Renaissance Party insists on calling it a lobby. Says it's less ostentatious and more socialist-y if that makes any sense."

Here, the forum was a large open ground as was typical, but with slightly more desks than was typical of city halls, and with something else unusual too. As they made their way to the center of the lobby, Terrasi suddenly pointed to the heavens. In the glass dome that formed the glorified skylight of the Municipio, a colossal, reddish-grey hammer and sickle hanged over them in a grand display, as if to tell to the wary visitor: Yes indeed, here is the International. The monument was made of stone, for metals were deemed too similar to the crude tastes of the feudal past, and on the hammer's handle were the names of the proud masons who helped construct the display. 

Notably, the surname Terrasi seems to appear quite a number of times, and Terrasi made it a point to note the names repeatedly to her guests. She then placed attention to some of the details on the huge monument. A side plaque detailing its purpose and date of installation, the intricate carvings into the hammer's handle and the sickle's blade. 

"My uncle's company supplied the granite for the hammer and sickle." She elaborated. "While a few cousins helped with the soapstone on the hammer's star. The whole thing took literally just a month to finish, y'know? I was there when it got installed, it was such a cool event too!"

"Mostly because you slept through Comrade Graci's speech and only woke up when everyone started applauding." A voice interrupted, walking up behind them. It was the man with the red hair, Argo Lo Pilato. Judging by his exasperated expression, it seems he did not expect his bespesctacled colleague to take matters into her own hands as a tour guide for the Thyvenic delegation. 

"I didn't sleep! The speech was just so bad that I looked like I was out cold!" 

"If you say so, Comrade Terrasi." Argo turned to the Thyvenics apologetically, bowing his head. "Gentlemen, I am Argo Lo Pilato, Chair of the Standing Council of the Patriciate for the Social Renaissance Party. I understand that you've arrived here on business concerning the Socialist International?"

[b]Marrin, Coastal Alliance Emergency Broadcast to the people of Tirakan and its allies[/b]

[Spoiler]

[i]*tfffft*[/i]
"Are we live?"
"In 3, 2, 1."
*on all TVs of Tirakan a woman in a simple shirt appears, all radios of the country stop playing music to announce the national broadcast. a deep breath before she speak*

"People of the coast. Citizens of Tirakan. Friends beyond our borders.
This is President Amina Velar, speaking from Marrin. Behind these walls, the guns of the Renaissance Union are sounding. Their tanks are on our hills. Their generals say this is the final day of the Coastal Alliance. They are wrong.

You have heard the voice of Nadir Suleiman in Valddera. You have heard him praise the very armies that are now shelling our hospitals, choking our trenches with gas, and driving families from the western districts of Marrin. You have heard him demand that we cut our own coastline away and gift it to a monarchist war machine as a bridgehead.

Let me answer him clearly, so there is no doubt in anyone listening to my words.
We will not surrender a single pier, a single street, a single child of this coast to a tyrannical crown or to a foreign government that treats our war like a bargaining chip. We are not a strip of land to be traded between generals. We are a people.

To the Renaissance Union, who wrap themselves in the old flag and call it legitimacy: you stand today not as restorers of order, but as the last defense of a failed age. You march with the blessing of outsiders who neither bled when Tirakan fell apart nor stood to watch over its waters. You are at Marrins gate because you could not win hearts, so you chose to break them.
To the Holy League, whose bombers murdered Premier Kareth Onu in cold blood: you speak of holy seas and yet drown cities in blood. You speak of faith and yet fear free minds so much that you kill those who dare to question you. Understand this: you have made enemies not only of the coast, but of every citizen of Tirakan who has buried a loved one for refusing your chains.
To the people of Valddera that hear this message, I speak past your leader and directly to you. Your sons and daughters are being asked to guard islands that do not belong to them, for the glory of a monarchy that is not theirs, against a people that never lifted arms against you. We do not seek your land. We do not seek your submission. We seek only that you do not lend your strength to those who would drag this entire region backwards.

And now, to Naerim.
Acting Premier Arlan Vos, to the brightest minds and toughest hearts of Naerim: our grief for Kareth Onu is still raw. The Holy League thought that by killing one man they could shatter an idea. They have only hardened it. Today, I announce publicly what we have already agreed in private.
From this hour, the Coastal Alliance and the Free Republic of Naerim stand in a formal defense pact.
Naerim air wings and naval groups are authorized to strike Renaissance Union artillery and armored concentrations threatening Marrin and the southern coastal corridor. Our harbors are open to Naerim relief and escort fleets. Our commands are linked. Our maps are shared. Where they try to break our line, we will answer together.

And most importantly, to our own people in Marrin and along the coast: we do not lie to you. The next days will be hard. Some of you will have to withdraw from forward trenches to secondary lines. Some streets will be lost. But hear me: where we must, we will fall back to fight again. I have already signed the orders to evacuate civilians behind the inner ring, to move field hospitals out of the immediate bombardment zone, and to keep our ports working long enough to receive every ship Naerim and our other friends can send.

If Marrins outer line breaks, we do not break. If the Renaissance Union plants its flag on one district, we reclaim three others in time.
But we seek no war beyond what we must fight to survive. To Valdderas navy I say this: stay outside our recognized coastal zones, and no Coastal Alliance ship will fire on you. Cross that line to enforce Suleimans demands, and you will not find a helpless coast, but people rising from every corner of this country.
And if the Renaissance Union and Holy League really desire to unite, they have to stop trying to unify Tirakan under a boot. When you are ready to talk about a Tirakan where no throne and no altar can dictate to every soul, our doors will open. Until then, our guns stay pointed at you.
People of the coast, lift your heads. The sky is not theirs. The sea is not theirs. This land is not theirs.

This is President Amina Velar, in Marrin under fire.
Hold you-"

[b]December 16, 2026: Territorial Reorganisation[/b]

Since early 2025, the armed forces of Thýven had held a slice of land within the Shamatine state of Sal-Baliz, formed following the fall of the terrorist group of the same name that had operated within the center of the continent where the kingdom of Sal-Baliz now sat. The land had been renamed to Izmyr by the Thývenic military command and had been delegated to be a condominium with the kingdom under the laws of said institution. 

However, as a year had passed without issue within the territory, and with the massive restructuring of the government in the mainland, it was decided that Thýven would formally cede the territory back to the kingdom of Sal-Baliz and withdraw the 20,000 troops it had there in order to prepare for the overall reorganisation of the armed forces that was planned. 

Thus on the morning of December 16th the First Council would release a joint statement declaring that: The restoration of order and stability within the region of Izmyr has been completed under the  provisions of the joint Sal-Baliz-Thýven treaty signed in mid-2025, as such the central government of Thýven shall withdraw fully its claim and its forces from the territory of Izmyr, granting total control to the government of the kingdom of Sal-Baliz. The withdrawal shall be completed by January 20, 2027 with all forces being re-stationed in our West Shamat base to the West of the kingdom of Sal-Baliz for reorganisation and re-deployment elsewhere,
